System blueprint

A decision dashboard with shared definitions

Connect agreed business data to a readable decision view. Define the numbers first, validate selected sources, and build dashboards that show appropriate context and help a named audience choose the next action.

Level 2Choose a capability

A dashboard can look convincing while sources, formulas, periods, and identities disagree. The useful work is to establish a trustworthy definition and data path before turning the results into charts and comparisons.

Useful outputs

  • A metric dictionary with formulas, source fields, owners, and limitations.
  • A selected data model and documented reconciliation checks.
  • A dashboard with agreed views, permissions, and refresh behaviour.
  • A review and maintenance guide with exception ownership.

Inputs we need

  • The reporting audience, decision questions, metric owners, and definition requirements.
  • Approved sources, sample records, identifiers, currencies, time zones, and periods.
  • Refresh expectations, access roles, reconciliation evidence, and publication ownership.
Level 3Explore a focus

Define the measures

Agree the audience, recurring decisions, metric formulas, source fields, units, and practical limits. Select only the comparisons and filters that support a useful review.

Level 4Inspect the detail

  • Publish only records that pass the agreed schema and reconciliation checks.
  • Flag delayed sources, incomplete refreshes, and changed definitions for investigation.
  • Apply viewing permissions and filters according to the approved audience model.
  • Approve each formula, denominator, reporting period, and cost scope with its owner.
  • Reconcile selected totals and inspect unexpected or missing records.
  • Review chart interpretation, attribution assumptions, and comparable periods before distribution.

Prepare reliable data

Connect approved sources, model records, and reconcile selected totals and identifiers. Make missing data, refresh delays, and quality exceptions visible before publication.

Human expertise

Own the judgment.

Metric owners define the business meaning and validate calculations. Analysts assess data quality and interpretation; leadership or operational owners decide what action follows the evidence.

AI assistance

Support the process.

AI may help organize requirements, prepare transformations, or draft commentary. Analysts validate joins, formulas, comparisons, and conclusions; the system does not invent explanations for a change.
